newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius business welcomes new policy measures.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius business welcomes new policy measures.

text.p: The Mauritian private sector on Wednesday welcomed Finance Minister Vasant Bunwaree's new economic policies designed to restore confidence in the island.
The the representative body for the private sectorcapex coordinating body of the local private sector, was ecstatic.

"The presentation of Dr Bunwaree in parliament suggesting a graduated approach, is positive and we think that the new vision of government is in the right direction," Francis Piat, president of the private sector's Joint Economic Council, told Reuters in an interview.
"It follows that we (private sector) will continue to play our role as we are concerned by the economic progress of Mauritius," Bunwaree added.

In his first major economic policy statement, Bunwaree focused on medium-term macroeconomic objectives for Mauritius, including economic growth between 5.5 and 6.5 percent over the next three years by stimulating investments and savings and an inflation target below 5.0 percent by the turn of the century.
Bunwaree also aimed at bringing a gradual reduction in the Indian Ocean island's budget deficit by cutting wastage, getting more value for money and through further reforms in the tax system.
"We think the new finance minister has clearly seen the priority objectives and he has established the different axes where actions are necessary," Piat said.

Bunwaree told parliament in his Tuesday speech, "Our nation has the potential and government the political will to attain these goals...we are a committed government that means business. We can only promise what we can deliver. I can assure the nation that we shall deliver what we promise."

Piat saw another reassuring signal in Bunwaree's decision not to implement a hotel and restaurant tax increase sought in a controversial 1996/97 budget presented in May by his predecessor Rundheersing Bheenick.
That budget was widely criticised for the tax measures and the government subsequently had to amend several of them.

"In the budget, there was a change in direction in the government's fiscal policy...this surprised the private sector with the taxes on the productive sectors of the economy and brought serious interrogations," Piat said.
"But the declaration of the finance minister (Bunwaree) has redefined the parameters," he added.
